newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court fines scandal crash truck driver.
newsitem.headline: Turk court fines scandal crash truck driver.

text.p: A Turkish truck driver on Monday became the only person convicted so far in a security scandal when he was found guilty of causing a car crash that unearthed links between leading officials and criminal gangs.

Anatolian news agency said Hasan Gokce was fined six million lira ($43) and made to pay 100 million lira ($720) in damages to relatives of those who died when his truck hit a car in the western town of Susurluk.
A senior policeman, a gangster wanted for murder and a former beauty queen died in the crash. Government MP Sedat Bucak, who also heads a Kurdish militia, was seriously injured.
The accident last November spurred a series of media reports that painted a murky picture of gangsters using state privileges to kill opponents, trade drugs and traffic in guns.
Former interior minister Mehmet Agar resigned after the accident when the media implicated him in the affair.
Only 10 people, mostly low-ranking policeman, have been charged by an Istanbul court investigating the scandal. They are due to go on trial next month.
A parliamentary commission report which implicated Bucak and Agar is to be debated in parliament on Tuesday.
